name: Drakeyard Pigment Crop Tank
description:
A cropped tank top in a garment-dyed cotton-analog that takes pigment in deep, slightly uneven washes — each batch comes out a little different, which is the point. Cut with a wide, low armhole and a straight hem that sits two inches above the waist. Neckline is a generous scoop. The fabric is lightweight but not sheer, with enough body to drape rather than cling. Common colors: acid-washed indigo, rust-dye terracotta, a particular muddy sage, and a near-black that fades to charcoal after washing.

Drakeyard is a street-level brand operating out of a dye workshop in the Tier 2/3 border corridor. The tanks are sold at popup markets, through a small network of independent boutiques, and via word of mouth. They have an outsized cultural footprint for their size — worn by musicians, athletes, and people who just want something that looks good without trying to look expensive. The crop is wearable on most bodies; the wide armhole accommodates augmented shoulder profiles naturally.
what_it_says: You know where to look. You're not buying into anything manufactured — you're buying into something made.
story_hooks: A specific dye batch from Drakeyard has been producing an unexpected bioluminescent afterglow in UV light — the dye source is unregistered and possibly geneware-derived.
The Drakeyard workshop is being pressured to relocate by a Tier 4 corridor development project; the owner is considering more direct forms of resistance.
A character tracking a missing person follows a trail of Drakeyard tanks — three people, all wearing the same rust-dye batch, all disappeared within a week of each other.

physical_description.visual_profile: A relaxed, effortlessly styled crop tank with generous proportions that reads as intentionally undone—sophisticated street wear with zero corporate polish. Sits confidently between athletic and avant-garde.
physical_description.fit: Straight-cut with a wide, low armhole that creates a relaxed shoulder line; crops two inches above the natural waist. Loose enough to breathe, structured enough to hold shape. Accommodates augmented frames without bunching.
physical_description.primary_material: Cotton-analog blend (synthetic cellulose base), garment-dyed to preserve natural variation and depth
physical_description.texture: Softly textured, lightweight with substantial hand-feel; uneven dye absorption creates subtle micro-variations in surface appearance that catch light differently across the garment
physical_description.color_scheme: Deep, moody colorways: acid-washed indigo with faded blue halos, rust-dye terracotta with burnt umber undertones, muddy sage with greenish-grey cast, or near-black that fades to charcoal at stress points and after repeated washing
distinctive_features: Hand-dyed batch variation—no two garments identical
Generous scoop neckline with soft edge
Extra-wide armhole that reads as intentional design, not oversizing
Cropped hem with clean, straight cut
Fabric retains slight sheen from dye process without being glossy
Natural fading and color shift visible after wear
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 2/3 crossover—too distinctive and artisanal for corpo uniform, too quality-conscious for sub-grade salvage
physical_description.cultural_context: Street musician, athlete, creative class—worn by people with personal style autonomy who reject both corpo branding and conspicuous poverty signaling. Strong subcultural cache without gatekeeping.
physical_description.condition_typical: Broken-in and softened after first few washes; color deepens slightly with wear; edges remain clean; occasional pull or soft crease from movement
